mainTopic: The New Years of ניסן and אלול: שקלים, house rentals, the authorship of the משנה's clauses, and why the עומר and שתי הלחם are not counted
overview: This amud opens by finishing an earlier answer: a ברייתא had to teach that an individual's donated קרבנות צבור are valid, even though we might worry he never fully handed them over. The גמרא explains that our משנה leaves out ניסן as the New Year for שקלים because that rule is not absolute: one who brings from the old collection is still יוצא. Next it discusses the יש אומרים who make ניסן the New Year for house rentals. It explains why a rental 'for this year' ends at ניסן and not תשרי, and why other תנאים disagree, since rain still falls in ניסן. The גמרא then turns to the משנה's clauses on רגלים and מעשר בהמה, which seem to follow different תנאים. רב יוסף says רבי picked different views for each topic, and רבא and רב נחמן בר יצחק explain how the משנה can still say 'four'. Finally, a ברייתא adds the עומר and שתי הלחם as New Years. רב פפא and רב שישא בריה דרב אידי each give a rule for why the משנה leaves them out, and each rule is defended against a challenge from רגלים, and רב פפא's rule also against one from יובל.

steps.title: Finishing the answer: we might fear he won't fully hand over the offerings
steps.stepSummary: This is the end of an earlier answer. The ברייתא had to teach that an individual's donated קרבנות צבור are valid once given to the public. Otherwise we might worry he won't hand them over wholeheartedly.
steps.simpleTranslation: [You might have thought we should worry that] he will not hand them over to the public completely and properly, so the ברייתא teaches us [that they are valid].
steps.whatsHappening: This amud begins in the middle of an answer that started earlier on the דף. The גמרא is finishing its explanation of why the ברייתא needed to state a rule that seemed obvious (פשיטא).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא asked: 'It is obvious that a private person can donate a communal offering if he hands it over to the public. Why say it?' The answer is that we might have feared he would secretly keep some ownership in his heart, which would make it not truly a communal offering. The ברייתא teaches us that this fear is not a concern.

keyTerms.meaning: He will hand them over (transfer ownership)
'It teaches us': the new point the source is coming to make

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new topic. It is the tail end of a מהו דתימא / קא משמע לן answer that began on the previous amud.

phrases.english: [lest] he will not hand them over to the public fully and properly,
phrases.notes: This finishes the 'מהו דתימא' (you might have said) idea that started a few lines back.

phrases.english: [therefore] it teaches us [that this is not a concern].
phrases.notes: This is the usual way the גמרא wraps up an answer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer to a פשיטא challenge raised on the previous amud.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא / קא משמע לן: shows the ruling is not obvious because of a possible worry
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have worried that a private donor would not fully give up ownership, so the offering would not count as communal.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא teaches that we do not worry about this; once he hands it to the public, it is valid as a communal offering.

steps.title: Why doesn't our משנה list ניסן as the New Year for שקלים?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists ניסן as the New Year for שקלים. The גמרא asks why the תנא of our משנה left this out.
steps.simpleTranslation: And our תנא [of the משנה], why did he not list it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question: the ברייתא includes שקלים among the things whose year starts in ניסן, so why does our משנה leave it out? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה at the start of the מסכתא lists ניסן as ראש השנה for kings and for festivals, but it does not mention שקלים. Since the ברייתא does count שקלים, the גמרא wants to know what the תנא of the משנה was thinking.

keyTerms.meaning: Our תנא, meaning the author of our משנה
The yearly half-shekel donation that funded the communal offerings

phrases.english: And our tanna [of the Mishnah — why did he not list shekels]?
phrases.notes: The גמרא asks this in just a couple of words, carrying the question over from what came before: why didn't our משנה list shekels?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having explained the ברייתא's rule about שקלים, the גמרא now compares it to the wording of our משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the משנה omits ניסן as the New Year for שקלים, when the ברייתא includes it.

steps.title: The שקלים New Year is not an absolute rule, so the משנה omits it
steps.stepSummary: Since one who brings offerings from the old collection is still יוצא, the ניסן cutoff for שקלים is not a firm rule. The משנה only lists firm New Years.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it is taught: 'If he brought [from the old collection], he has fulfilled his obligation,' it is not a definite rule for him [so he did not list it].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. Our משנה only lists New Years that are firm and absolute, and the New Year for שקלים is not absolute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Communal offerings should come from the new collection starting in ניסן. But if they came from the old collection, they still count (יצא). Because the ניסן boundary is only the ideal (a מצוה) and not a requirement, the תנא could not state it as a clear-cut rule (פסיקא).

keyTerms.meaning: If he brought [from the old], he fulfilled his obligation
The old collection of שקלים from the previous year (implied)
It is not clear-cut or absolute for him

steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה lists only absolute New Years. The ניסן New Year for שקלים is only the ideal, since after the fact old funds still work, so the משנה leaves it out.

phrases.english: Since it is taught: If he brought [from the old collection], he has fulfilled [his obligation] —
phrases.notes: Quoting the ברייתא about bringing communal offerings from the old collection.

phrases.english: it is not a definite [rule] for him.
phrases.notes: So the תנא of the משנה, who lists only fixed rules, omits it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה lists only absolute New Years. The שקלים deadline is not absolute, because using old funds is valid after the fact, so it was left out.

steps.title: Some say ניסן is also the New Year for renting houses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא: the יש אומרים view that ניסן is also the New Year for house rentals.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And some say: also for the renting of houses.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new piece of the ברייתא and quotes it so it can explain it. This step sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא had listed ניסן as the New Year for months, leap years, and שקלים. The יש אומרים add rental contracts. The גמרא is about to show what practical difference this makes.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say: an additional opinion

phrases.english: And some say: [Nisan is] also [the New Year] for the renting of houses.
phrases.notes: A quote from the ברייתא, introducing a new topic.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the topic of שקלים to the next clause of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the יש אומרים, ניסן begins the year for house rental contracts.

steps.title: Renting 'for a year' versus 'for this year'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains the rental rule. Renting 'for a year' means twelve full months. Renting 'for this year' ends on א' ניסן, even if the rental began only on א' אדר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: If one rents a house to his friend 'for a year,' he counts twelve months from day to day. But if he said 'for this year,' even if [the deal] was made only on the first of אדר, once the first of ניסן arrives, the year is finished for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that shows exactly how ניסן works as the New Year for rentals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'A year' with no further detail means a full twelve months from the day the rental began. 'This year' means the current calendar year, which ends when ניסן arrives. So someone who rented on א' אדר gets only one month. This is the practical meaning of the יש אומרים.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן taught: introduces a ברייתא
From day to day: a full count from the start date
The year is counted as complete for him

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two phrasings. 'לשנה' means twelve months from the start date. 'לשנה זו' means until the calendar year ends at ניסן.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the exact wording of a contract decides its length. ניסן is the cutoff only when the parties tie the rental to the calendar year.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
phrases.notes: Introduces a ברייתא.

phrases.english: One who rents a house to his fellow for a year —

phrases.aramaic: מוֹנֶה שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חוֹדֶשׁ מִיּוֹם לְיוֹם.
phrases.english: counts twelve months from day to day.
But if he said 'for this year,'

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ לֹא עָמַד אֶלָּא בְּאֶחָד בַּאֲדָר,
phrases.english: even if [the deal] was made only on the first of Adar,
once the first day of Nisan arrives —
the year is completed for him.
phrases.notes: The rental ends; ניסן starts a new year.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַמַּשְׂכִּיר בַּיִת לַחֲבֵירוֹ לְשָׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the practical meaning of the יש אומרים quoted in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'For a year' means twelve full months. 'For this year' ends on א' ניסן, even if the rental began only a month earlier, on א' אדר.

steps.title: Rentals are different: no one rents for less than thirty days
steps.stepSummary: Even the view that one day in a year counts as a year agrees that rentals are different. People do not rent a house for less than thirty days, so a few days of אדר do not count as 'this year'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even according to the one who says that one day in a year counts as a year, here it is different, because a person does not bother to rent a house for less than thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an unspoken question. Why did the ברייתא say 'א' אדר', and not a later date? It explains that a rental is a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Elsewhere we learn that יום אחד בשנה חשוב שנה, so we might think that even one day before ניסן ends 'this year'. But people do not rent for under thirty days. So if someone rents with fewer than thirty days left before ניסן, he surely meant the coming year. That is why the ברייתא chose א' אדר, which is a full thirty days before ניסן.

keyTerms.meaning: One day in a year counts as a [whole] year
A person does not take the trouble

steps.whatToRemember: For a 'this year' rental, ניסן ends the contract only if at least thirty days remain before it. With fewer days left, the renter is assumed to mean the coming year, because no one rents a house for under thirty days.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that halachic definitions of time can bend to normal human behavior (דעת בני אדם) when we are interpreting a contract.

phrases.english: And even according to the one who says
one day in a year counts as a year —
phrases.notes: A principle discussed earlier in the מסכתא regarding the years of kings.

phrases.english: here it is different,
because a person does not take the trouble
to rent a house for less than thirty days.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ לְמַאן דְּאָמַר יוֹם אֶחָד בַּשָּׁנָה חָשׁוּב שָׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the ברייתא in step 5 used א' אדר and limits how far the rule reaches.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction (שאני הכא): rental contracts follow ordinary human practice
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Based on יום אחד בשנה חשוב שנה, we might think that even renting one day before ניסן would end 'this year' at ניסן.
steps.terutzMaskana: Rentals are different: people do not rent for under thirty days, so 'this year' ends at ניסן only if at least thirty days remain.

steps.title: Why not make תשרי the cutoff for rentals?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a 'this year' rental does not end at תשרי instead of ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why not say תשרי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the rental year should end at ניסן and not at תשרי. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תשרי is the usual start of the year for many things, like years and שמיטה. So it seems more natural for 'this year' in a rental to end at תשרי. The גמרא wants to know why the יש אומרים chose ניסן.

phrases.english: But why not say Tishrei?
phrases.notes: Why not make Tishrei the end point of a 'this year' rental?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the rental rule from steps 4-6 picks ניסן as the cutoff.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is ניסן, not תשרי, the end point of a 'this year' rental?

steps.title: People rent for the whole rainy season
steps.stepSummary: A person who rents without saying how long means to rent for the full rainy season, which ends around ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: When a person rents a house without saying how long, he rents it for the whole rainy season.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that people rent houses to have shelter for the whole rainy season. That season ends around ניסן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rentals follow how people actually think. Ending at תשרי would cut the renter off just as the rains start. Ending at ניסן fits a rental that covers the whole winter.

phrases.english: Ordinarily, when a person rents a house without saying how long,
he rents it for the whole rainy season.
phrases.notes: The rainy season ends around ניסן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Rentals are meant to cover the whole rainy season, so ניסן, not תשרי, is the natural end.

steps.title: Why do other תנאים leave out rentals?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the תנא קמא of the ברייתא and our משנה do not list ניסן as the New Year for rentals.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the first תנא of the ברייתא, and our תנא, why do they not list it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why some תנאים do not list rentals as a ניסן New Year. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 explained why ניסן makes sense for rentals. So the גמרא now asks why the תנא קמא of the ברייתא and our משנה did not include this rule in their lists.

keyTerms.meaning: The first תנא, whose view is stated first
A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה
Our תנא, the author of our משנה

phrases.english: And the first Tanna of the Baraita,
and our Tanna, why do they leave it out?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining the יש אומרים, asks why the other תנאים do not share it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why do the תנא קמא and our משנה not list rentals under ניסן?

steps.title: Clouds and rain are still common in ניסן
steps.stepSummary: Rain still falls in ניסן, so the rainy season does not clearly end on א' ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even in ניסן, clouds are commonly found.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that rain is still common in ניסן. So a renter would not want his rental to end exactly on א' ניסן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sides agree that a renter wants the whole rainy season. They disagree about when that season really ends. Since rain continues into ניסן, א' ניסן is not a firm end, so these תנאים do not list it.
steps.whatToRemember: The יש אומרים end rentals at ניסן because that is when the rainy season ends. The other תנאים disagree because rain still falls in ניסן.

phrases.english: Even in Nisan, rain clouds are commonly found.
phrases.notes: So the renter still needs shelter after א' ניסן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9 and closes the rental discussion.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Rain continues into ניסן, so א' ניסן is not a clear end of the rental period.

steps.title: The אלול New Year for animal tithes follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה and says the clause about מעשר בהמה on א' אלול follows רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the first of אלול is the New Year for animal tithes. Whose view is this? It is רבי מאיר, as it was taught: רבי מאיר says, on the first of אלול is the New Year for animal tithes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next clause of the משנה, about מעשר בהמה. It shows that this clause follows רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא proves the author by quoting a teaching in which רבי מאיר says exactly these words. This identification sets up a problem that comes up in steps 12-13.

keyTerms.meaning: The tithe of animals: every tenth animal is set aside

phrases.aramaic: בְּאֶחָד בֶּאֱלוּל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לְמַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה.
phrases.english: On the first of Elul is the New Year for animal tithes.
phrases.notes: Quoted from the משנה.

phrases.english: Whose view is this? It is Rabbi Meir.
As it was taught: Rabbi Meir says:

phrases.aramaic: בְּאֶחָד בֶּאֱלוּל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לְמַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה.
phrases.english: On the first of Elul is the New Year for animal tithes.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּאֶחָד בֶּאֱלוּל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לְמַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה. מַנִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's א' אלול New Year for מעשר בהמה follows רבי מאיר.

steps.title: The Festivals clause follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the משנה's opening clause, about ניסן as the New Year for רגלים, follows רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the clause about the Festivals: whose view is it? It is רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the משנה's first clause, about רגלים, follows רבי שמעון. This sets up the problem in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא showed that ניסן as the New Year for רגלים follows רבי שמעון. That is the rule for the prohibition of delaying vows (בל תאחר), which applies only after the Festivals pass in order, starting from פסח. Now the first clause and the middle clause seem to follow two different תנאים.

phrases.english: And 'for the Festivals': whose view is it? It is Rabbi Shimon.
phrases.notes: Refers to the משנה's first clause about ניסן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second author identification, which together with step 11 creates a problem.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The רגלים clause of the משנה follows רבי שמעון.

steps.title: Can the משנה switch authors in the middle?
steps.stepSummary: The last clause names רבי שמעון for תשרי. So the first and last clauses follow רבי שמעון, but the middle clause follows רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say the last clause: רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון say, on the first of תשרי. So the first and last clauses follow רבי שמעון, and the middle clause follows רבי מאיר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a problem: the משנה seems to jump from רבי שמעון to רבי מאיר and back to רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's last clause says רבי שמעון holds that the New Year for מעשר בהמה is א' תשרי. So he cannot also be the author of the unnamed middle clause, which says א' אלול. A משנה that switches authors in the middle is very hard to accept.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'רישא' means the משנה's opening clause about רגלים in ניסן. It does not mean the line right before the אלול clause.

phrases.english: Say the last clause:
Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon say:
On the first of Tishrei.
phrases.notes: The New Year for animal tithes.

phrases.english: So the first clause and the last clause follow Rabbi Shimon,
and the middle clause follows Rabbi Meir!

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישָׁא וְסֵיפָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, וּמְצִיעֲתָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Combines the two identifications of steps 11-12 into a challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: How the author of the משנה's clauses is identified
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון himself holds תשרי for מעשר בהמה, so the unnamed אלול clause in the middle cannot be his. The משנה would then switch authors from clause to clause, which is very unlikely.

steps.title: רבי wrote the משנה and picked different opinions for different topics
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the משנה is רבי's. רבי follows רבי שמעון on רגלים and רבי מאיר on מעשר בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: It is רבי, and he takes the position of different תנאים. On רגלים he holds like רבי שמעון, and on מעשר בהמה he holds like רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the problem from step 13. The משנה seemed to jump between two תנאים, and he explains why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is not following one תנא from start to finish. רבי, who edited the משנה, decided the halacha topic by topic. So the mix is on purpose. It is not a contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: It is רבי (רבי יהודה הנשיא), the editor of the משנה
he takes it, meaning he adopts a position

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי is a third opinion arguing with both. He agrees with רבי שמעון on one topic and with רבי מאיר on another.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
It is Rebbi (Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi),
and he takes it according to different tanna'im.
phrases.notes: He picks the view of a different תנא for each topic.

phrases.english: Regarding the Festivals, he holds like Rabbi Shimon,

phrases.aramaic: וּבְמַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.english: and regarding animal tithes, he holds like Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 13 about the משנה mixing two תנאים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attribution to a third editor who rules topic by topic
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה must follow one תנא throughout, so a mix looks like a contradiction.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי intentionally chose רבי שמעון for רגלים and רבי מאיר for מעשר בהמה.

steps.title: If so, there should be five New Years, not four
steps.stepSummary: If רבי mixes both views, the total comes to five New Years, but the משנה says four.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, how can it say four? There are five!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב יוסף's answer. Mixing the two views gives too many New Years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each תנא has his own list. If רבי takes רגלים from רבי שמעון and מעשר בהמה (א' אלול) from רבי מאיר, he keeps an item from each list. Together that makes five dates. That clashes with the משנה's opening word 'four'.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, meaning if your answer is right
four, the number the משנה opens with

phrases.english: If so, [how can it say] four?
There are five!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's answer from step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that רבי mixed the opinions of רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Combining an item from each תנא's list produces five New Years. That contradicts the משנה's explicit count of four.

steps.title: Each תנא alone has only four
steps.stepSummary: רבא says 'four' is true for each opinion separately. רבי מאיר drops רגלים, and רבי שמעון drops מעשר בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Four according to everyone. For רבי מאיר there are four, since you remove רגלים. For רבי שמעון there are four, since you remove מעשר בהמה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends רב יוסף. He explains that the number four still works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's 'four' does not count the combined list. It means each תנא, on his own, has four New Years. רבי מאיר has no New Year for רגלים. For רבי שמעון, מעשר בהמה falls on א' תשרי, which is already on the list. So each list stays at four.

keyTerms.meaning: according to everyone, meaning each opinion

phrases.english: Rava said:
Four according to everyone;
according to Rabbi Meir, four: remove the Festivals,

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אַרְבָּעָה — דַּל מַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה.
phrases.english: according to Rabbi Shimon, four: remove animal tithes.
phrases.notes: For רבי שמעון it is on א' תשרי, which is already listed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the number in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Four' counts the total of the combined list.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Four' is the count within each תנא's own system.

steps.title: Four months, with several New Years inside them
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers differently. The משנה counts four months, and some months have more than one New Year.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: There are four months, and within them are several New Years.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a second, different answer to the קשיא of 'five'. The 'four' counts months, not New Years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא kept 'four' as a count of New Years for each תנא. רב נחמן בר יצחק changes what is being counted. Four months host the New Years. One month, ניסן, can hold two of them, so five New Years still fit into four months.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
four months
and within them are several New Years.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: אַרְבָּעָה חֳדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative to רבא's answer to step 15.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Four' counts months, and one month can contain several New Years.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists two more New Years, the עומר and the שתי הלחם
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא adds 16 ניסן (עומר) and 6 סיון (שתי הלחם). By רבא the משנה should say six. By רב נחמן בר יצחק it should say five.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: The sixteenth of ניסן is the New Year for the עומר. The sixth of סיון is the New Year for the שתי הלחם. By רבא, let it teach six. By רב נחמן בר יצחק, let it teach five.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge both answers at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא adds two New Years. That breaks רבא's count, since four plus two makes six. It also breaks רב נחמן בר יצחק's count, because סיון is a new month, so the months become five. Each answer seems to give the wrong number.

keyTerms.meaning: they challenged, using a source from the תנאים
the barley offering on 16 ניסן that permits the new grain
the two wheat loaves brought on שבועות

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next move. The גמרא will have to explain why the משנה does not count the עומר and the שתי הלחם as New Years.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: שִׁשָּׁה עָשָׂר בְּנִיסָן — רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לָעוֹמֶר.
phrases.english: The sixteenth of Nisan is the New Year for the omer.

phrases.aramaic: שִׁשָּׁה בְּסִיוָן — רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לִשְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם.
phrases.english: The sixth of Sivan is the New Year for the two loaves.
According to Rava, let it teach six,

phrases.aramaic: לְרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק לִיתְנֵי חֲמִשָּׁה?
phrases.english: according to Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak, let it teach five?
phrases.notes: סיון adds a fifth month.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: שִׁשָּׁה עָשָׂר בְּנִיסָן רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לָעוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges both answers from steps 16 and 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's count of four New Years per תנא, and רב נחמן בר יצחק's count of four months
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא adds two New Years, making six for רבא. It also adds the month of סיון, making five for רב נחמן בר יצחק.

steps.title: רב פפא: Only New Years that begin at night are counted
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers the challenge from the ברייתא. The משנה only counts New Years that take effect from the evening. The עומר and שתי הלחם take effect only when they are offered during the day, so they are left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: When the משנה counts, it counts things that take effect from the evening. Things that do not take effect from the evening, it does not count.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא explains why the משנה does not list the עומר and the שתי הלחם as New Years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every New Year in the משנה starts from nightfall at the beginning of its date. The עומר and שתי הלחם only take effect when they are actually brought, and that happens by day. That difference in timing is the reason the משנה leaves them out.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
When [the Mishnah] counts,
[it counts] something that takes effect from the evening.
phrases.notes: The New Year starts at nightfall.

phrases.english: Something that does not take effect from the evening
phrases.notes: Such as the עומר and שתי הלחם, which take effect only once offered by day.

phrases.english: it does not count.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: כִּי קָא חָשֵׁיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא of עומר and שתי הלחם
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines what the משנה chose to count
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה should have listed every New Year, including עומר and שתי הלחם
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה lists only New Years that begin at nightfall. עומר and שתי הלחם begin only by day.

steps.title: Challenge: The festivals do not begin at night either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב פפא. The New Year for רגלים does not seem to take effect at night, yet the משנה counts it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there are the רגלים, which do not take effect from the evening, and the משנה counts them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב פפא's rule with a counter-example from the משנה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The New Year for רגלים is about the prohibition of בל תאחר (delaying vowed offerings). Offerings cannot be brought at night, so a person cannot really be late until the morning. That makes it look like a New Year that starts by day, which contradicts רב פפא's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: But behold / but there is (introduces a counter-example)
The pilgrimage festivals (for counting בל תאחר)
The prohibition against delaying vowed offerings

phrases.english: But there are the Festivals,
which do not take effect from the evening,
phrases.notes: Offerings cannot be brought at night, so the delay is only violated in the morning.

phrases.english: and [the Mishnah] counts them!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲרֵי רְגָלִים, דְּלָא חָיְילִי מֵאוּרְתָּא, וְקָחָשֵׁיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's rule
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's rule that only New Years beginning at night are counted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רגלים seem to take effect only in the morning, yet the משנה counts them

steps.title: Answer: The obligation is already in place from the start of the festival
steps.stepSummary: Since the person must bring his offering by the festival, the obligation is already in force from the very start of the festival, which is the evening.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since he has to bring it from the beginning, he stands obligated already.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב פפא by explaining that רגלים really do take effect from the evening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He cannot physically offer at night, but the obligation to bring the offering already applies from the start of the רגל. So the 'New Year' for רגלים does begin at night, and רב פפא's rule stands.

phrases.english: Since he needs to bring [his offering] from the beginning [of the Festival],
he already stands obligated.
phrases.notes: The obligation starts at the evening, even though the actual offering waits for morning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רגלים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רגלים take effect only in the morning, when offerings can be brought
steps.terutzMaskana: The obligation is already in force from the evening, so רגלים fit רב פפא's rule

steps.title: Challenge: The Jubilee does not begin at night either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב פפא again. יובל starts with the שופר blast on יום כיפור, which happens by day, yet the משנה counts it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there are the יובלות, which do not take effect from the evening, and the משנה counts them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second counter-example against רב פפא, this time from יובל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The יובל takes effect through the שופר blast on יום כיפור, and that happens during the day. So it looks like another New Year in the משנה that does not start at night.

keyTerms.meaning: The שופר blast (on יום כיפור of the יובל year)

phrases.english: But there are the Jubilee years,
which do not take effect from the evening,
phrases.notes: They take effect from the שופר blast on יום כיפור during the day.

phrases.english: and [the Mishnah] counts them!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲרֵי יוֹבְלוֹת, דְּלָא חָיְילִי מֵאוּרְתָּא, וְקָחָשֵׁיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to רב פפא, built the same way as the first
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: יובל begins by day with the שופר, yet the משנה counts it

steps.title: Answer: The משנה follows the view that the יובל begins on ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה follows רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא, who holds that יובל already takes effect from ראש השנה, which begins at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is the view of רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא, who said: יובל takes effect from ראש השנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב פפא by saying the משנה follows a תנא who holds יובל starts on ראש השנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא, יובל starts on ראש השנה. The שופר on יום כיפור only finishes the process of freeing slaves and returning fields. Since ראש השנה starts at nightfall, יובל fits רב פפא's rule.

keyTerms.term: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָא
keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who holds יובל begins on ראש השנה
It is [the view of]; it ties the משנה to a specific תנא

steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא's rule (only New Years that begin at night are counted) survives both challenges. רגלים count because the obligation starts at night. יובל counts because the משנה follows the view that it begins on ראש השנה.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָא הִיא,
phrases.english: It is [the view of] Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka,
who said: The Jubilee takes effect from Rosh Hashanah.
phrases.notes: The שופר on יום כיפור only completes it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from יובל
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the משנה to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יובל begins by day with the שופר
steps.terutzMaskana: According to this תנא, יובל begins on ראש השנה at night

steps.title: רב שישא: Only New Years that do not depend on an action are counted
steps.stepSummary: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי gives a different answer. The משנה only counts New Years that happen automatically. The עומר and שתי הלחם depend on actually bringing them, so they are left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי said: When the משנה counts, it counts things that do not depend on an action. Things that depend on an action, it does not count.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא offers his own explanation for why the עומר and שתי הלחם are missing from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב שישא's rule is not about timing at all. It is about whether a human action is needed. Every New Year in the משנה comes automatically with the calendar date. The עומר and שתי הלחם only permit the new grain once someone actually offers them.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives a second answer

steps.confusionAlert: רב שישא is not adding to רב פפא's rule. He replaces it with a different reason. רב פפא asks 'Does it begin at night?' and רב שישא asks 'Does it need a human action?'

phrases.aramaic: רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Sheisha, son of Rav Idi, said:
When [the Mishnah] counts,
[it counts] something that does not depend on an action;
something that depends on an action
phrases.notes: Such as offering the עומר or the שתי הלחם.

phrases.english: it does not count.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי אָמַר: כִּי קָא חָשֵׁיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: An alternative answer to the challenge in step 18, in place of רב פפא's answer
steps.terutzResolutionType: A different rule for what the משנה chose to count
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The עומר and שתי הלחם should be counted as New Years
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה lists only automatic New Years. The עומר and שתי הלחם depend on being offered.

steps.title: The New Year for festivals seems to depend on an action
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב שישא בריה דרב אידי. The New Year for רגלים seems to depend on an action, yet the משנה counts it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about the festivals? That is something that depends on an action, and yet the משנה counts it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rule just given by רב שישא בריה דרב אידי. That rule said the משנה only counts New Years that happen automatically.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב שישא said the עומר and שתי הלחם were left out because they depend on an action. The גמרא points out that רגלים also seems to depend on an action, and the משנה still counts it. If that is true, his rule does not explain the list.

keyTerms.meaning: The three pilgrimage festivals: פסח, שבועות, and סוכות
Something that depends on an action being done
He (the תנא of the משנה) counts it

phrases.english: But there are the festivals,
phrases.notes: Refers to the משנה's New Year for רגלים, the starting point for the prohibition of delaying vows.

phrases.english: something that depends on an action,
phrases.notes: This means offering the daily תמיד, since no offering may be brought before it.

phrases.english: and yet he counts it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲרֵי רְגָלִים מִידֵּי דִּתְלֵי בְּמַעֲשֶׂה וְקָא חָשֵׁיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rule set up in Step 24 (only automatic New Years are counted).
steps.kashyaTarget: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי's rule that the משנה lists only New Years that take effect automatically
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Counterexample: רגלים seems to depend on an action, yet it appears in the משנה's list.

steps.title: The ban on delaying takes effect by itself
steps.stepSummary: The prohibition of בל תאחר takes effect automatically when the festival comes. So the New Year for רגלים does not depend on an action.
steps.simpleTranslation: The prohibition 'Do not delay' takes effect by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב שישא. It says the New Year for רגלים does not really depend on any action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The New Year for רגלים is about the prohibition of בל תאחר, the ban on delaying a promised offering. That prohibition begins the moment the festival arrives, whether or not anyone brings an offering. So it fits the rule of New Years that happen automatically, unlike the עומר and שתי הלחם.

keyTerms.meaning: The prohibition 'Do not delay' paying a vowed offering

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב שישא, the משנה lists only New Years that start automatically. רגלים qualifies because בל תאחר begins the moment the festival comes. The עומר and שתי הלחם do not qualify because they depend on actually being brought.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up 'bringing the offering' with 'the prohibition starting.' Bringing the offering is an action. The prohibition starts automatically, and that is what the משנה is counting.

phrases.english: 'You shall not delay'
takes effect on its own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 25 and protects רב שישא's rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining what the New Year for רגלים is about: the automatic prohibition, not the action of offering
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The New Year for רגלים depends on the action of offering sacrifices, so it should not be counted.
steps.terutzMaskana: The New Year for רגלים is defined by the בל תאחר prohibition, which takes effect automatically. So it rightly belongs in the משנה.
